app.name: Trees vs Breath
app.tagline: Test a street's trees before anyone plants them.
theme.label: Theme
footer.simulated: Every model number in this app is simulated and tagged as such.
start.question: Plant a tree — cooler street or dirtier air?
start.lede: In a narrow Hong Kong street, a tree can shade the pavement and still make the air at your nose dirtier. Test the street before anyone plants.
start.method: AI proposes, physics verifies, the wind tunnel judges.
start.illustration: Illustration of an example street with assumed dimensions. The live simulation arrives in phase 1.
section.title: Cross-section of a street canyon
street.title: Street
street.intro: Choose one of three example streets or enter your own: building height, street width, pavements and compass direction. Phone mode measures them with a compass, a tilt reading and a tape.
design.title: Design
design.intro: Wind blows across a street from the left. Change the street's shape and watch how the air turns inside it.
tradeOff.title: Trade-off
tradeOff.intro: Every design the AI swept, plotted as heat against fumes. A design on the frontier cannot get cooler without its air getting dirtier.
compare.title: Compare
compare.intro: Up to four designs side by side, with the one we would choose and the reason.
howWeKnow.title: How we know
howWeKnow.intro: The checks behind every number: solver benchmarks, the wind-tunnel reference case, direction checks against published studies, and the AI's accuracy.
leftOut.3d: 3D effects such as junctions, short streets and wind along the street
leftOut.chemistry: NO–NO₂–O₃ chemistry (the fumes are a passive tracer)
hongKong.title: Hong Kong
hongKong.intro: Roadside air quality and summer heat stress in Hong Kong, and how the city already assesses air ventilation for large developments.
report.title: Report
report.intro: A one-page printable summary for a district council or a residents' group.
present.title: Presentation mode
present.intro: A full-screen guided story for the four-minute pitch, stepped with the arrow keys or a clicker.
notFound.title: Page not found
design.simLabel: Live simulation of wind blowing across a street between two buildings
design.aspect: Street shape: building height ÷ street width (H/W)
design.aspectHint: Narrow streets between tall buildings have a high H/W.
design.expected: What published studies lead us to expect
design.next: Trees, hedges and traffic fumes come next, in phase 2.
regime.isolatedBody: The buildings are far apart; each disturbs the wind on its own.
regime.wakeBody: The wake behind the upwind building runs into the windward building.
regime.skimmingBody: The wind skims over the roofs and drives one vortex trapped in the street.
regime.deepBody: The trapped air splits into vortices stacked one above the other; the lower one turns slowly.
regime.sourceLiu: Two stacked vortices at H/W 2 in the simulations of Liu, Barth and Leung (2004).
readout.reynoldsHelp: Reynolds number: inflow speed × building height ÷ the model air's viscosity. Real streets have much higher values; this is listed under what the model leaves out.
engineNote.noWebgpu: This browser has no WebGPU, so the simulation runs on the CPU at a coarser grid.
engineNote.webgpuFailed: WebGPU failed to start, so the simulation runs on the CPU at a coarser grid.
engineNote.gpuLost: The GPU stopped responding, so the simulation moved to the CPU.
evidence.pendingBody: This check has not been run yet. Its result appears here once the pipeline writes it to results/.
hwk.solverIntro: Before the solver is trusted in a street, it has to reproduce flows whose answers are known.
hwk.poisQuestion: Does the solver match the exact profile of flow driven between two plates (Poiseuille)? Target: error below {tol} with {h} cells across or more.
hwk.cavityTitle: Box with a moving lid, Reynolds number {re}
hwk.cavityQuestion: Does the solver reproduce the reference solution of Ghia, Ghia and Shin (1982)? Target: within {tol} of the lid speed.
hwk.cavityChart: Horizontal velocity along the vertical centre line
hwk.massQuestion: In a closed box no air may appear or vanish. Target: change below {tol}.
hwk.lesQuestion: Does the sub-grid model add exactly the eddy viscosity it should (Smagorinsky), with the effect of body forces removed?
hwk.agreeTitle: The same answer on every device
hwk.agreeQuestion: A phone runs the solver on its GPU or CPU; the reference runs in Python. Do they agree? Target: within {tol} of the reference speed.
hwk.agreeJax: The JAX version that runs on the A100 agrees with NumPy to within {worst} of the reference speed.
hwk.streetIntro: The street flow has to show the structures that field studies and other models report.
hwk.regimeTitle: How the air turns as the street narrows
hwk.regimeQuestion: In wide streets the wind reaches the ground; in narrower streets one vortex is trapped; in deep streets vortices stack (Oke 1988; Liu, Barth and Leung 2004). Does the model show this?
hwk.regimeKey: Lines: time-averaged streamlines inside the street, wind from the left. Dots: vortex centres, named from top to bottom.
regimes.plotLabel: Streamlines in a street with H/W {aspect}: {n} stacked vortex cells
hwk.spongeTitle: Sound kept out of the street
hwk.spongeQuestion: Vortices shed by the buildings make sound, which can bounce around the model and drown the real pressure changes. Absorbing layers at the edges should remove it.
hwk.spongeChart: Pressure noise in the street over time
hwk.stabQuestion: Which combinations of Reynolds number and Smagorinsky constant run without blowing up? The live street uses Reynolds number {re} with Cs {cs}.
hwk.later: The wind-tunnel comparison (CODASC), the direction checks for trees and hedges, and the sun and heat checks are added in phases 2 to 4.
hwk.check.skimming: Skimming flow: one vortex fills the street (Oke 1988; Liu, Barth and Leung 2004). Observed: {n} vortex cells, {floor} of the floor with the wind.
hwk.check.rotation: The vortex turns with the wind above the roofs: clockwise for wind from the left. Observed: {rotation}; top of the street moving at {top} × the inflow speed.
hwk.check.stacked: Two vortices stacked one above the other, turning in opposite directions (Liu, Barth and Leung 2004). Observed: {n} stacked cells.
hwk.check.wake: Outside skimming flow (H/W below 0.7, Oke 1988) the outer flow reaches the street floor. Observed: {floor} of the floor with the wind.
hwk.check.deep: Very deep street: at least two stacked vortices. Observed: {n} stacked cells.
hwk.upwindTitle: Why the model street has a street upwind
hwk.upwindQuestion: In a flat (2D) model, the vortex shed by the first building's upwind edge stays over the street behind it. Does one street upwind give the studied street the skimming flow seen in wind tunnels and city blocks?
hwk.upwindTop: top of the street ÷ inflow speed
hwk.upwindChart: Time-averaged wind across the middle of the street
hwk.upwindNote: Positive values move with the wind. Under skimming flow the top of the street moves with the wind and the floor against it.
